claim: Mutations in members of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling family are common events in cancer.
source: Mutations in members of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling family are common events in cancer, but the mechanisms whereby disruption of SWI/SNF components alters tumorigenesis remain poorly understood.
evidence: This is a general statement about the prevalence of SWI/SNF mutations in cancer, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: The mechanisms whereby disruption of SWI/SNF components alters tumorigenesis remain poorly understood.
source: Mutations in members of the SWI/SNF chromatin remodeling family are common events in cancer, but the mechanisms whereby disruption of SWI/SNF components alters tumorigenesis remain poorly understood.
evidence: This statement identifies a knowledge gap in the field regarding SWI/SNF function in cancer.

claim: Arid1a cooperates with Kras in the adult pancreas as postnatal silencing of Arid1a following sustained KrasG12D expression induces rapid and irreversible reprogramming of acinar cells into mucinous PDAC precursor lesions.
source: Arid1a cooperates with Kras in the adult pancreas as postnatal silencing of Arid1a following sustained KrasG12D expression induces rapid and irreversible reprogramming of acinar cells into mucinous PDAC precursor lesions.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data from the mouse model.

claim: Arid1a silencing during embryogenesis, concurrent with KrasG12D activation, leads to retention of acinar cell fate.
source: In contrast, Arid1a silencing during embryogenesis, concurrent with KrasG12D activation, leads to retention of acinar cell fate.
evidence: This is a primary finding demonstrating context-dependent effects of Arid1a loss, supported by experimental data.

claim: Arid1a is a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity.
source: Together, our results demonstrate Arid1a as a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity, and underscore an unanticipated influence of timing and genetic context on the effects of SWI/SNF complex alterations in epithelial tumorigenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: Timing and genetic context influence the effects of SWI/SNF complex alterations in epithelial tumorigenesis.
source: Together, our results demonstrate Arid1a as a critical modulator of Kras-dependent changes in acinar cell identity, and underscore an unanticipated influence of timing and genetic context on the effects of SWI/SNF complex alterations in epithelial tumorigenesis.
evidence: This conclusion is based on the differential phenotypes observed when Arid1a is suppressed at different developmental timepoints.

claim: Aberrant chromatin regulation is a hallmark of cancer.
source: Aberrant chromatin regulation is a hallmark of cancer (Flavahan et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Mutations in genes encoding chromatin readers, writers and remodelers have been detected across the spectrum of human cancers.
source: Numerous studies have revealed an abnormal chromatin state in tumor cells in comparison with their tissue of origin, and mutations in genes encoding chromatin readers, writers and remodelers have been detected across the spectrum of human cancers (Feinberg et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Subunits of the SWI/SNF ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling complex show frequent mutation in many solid tumors.
source: For example, subunits of the SWI/SNF ATP-dependent chromatin-remodeling complex show frequent mutation in many solid tumors (Bailey et al., 2016; Waddell et al., 2015; Witkiewicz et al., 2015), but understanding of the underlying biology and molecular mechanisms as to how these mutations influence cancer related processes remains limited.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: SWI/SNF complexes regulate chromatin accessibility and gene expression by re-positioning nucleosomes and interacting with available transcription factors at enhancer regions.
source: SWI/SNF complexes regulate chromatin accessibility and thus gene expression by re-positioning nucleosomes and interacting with available transcription factors (TFs) at enhancer regions (Kelso et al., 2017; Mathur et al., 2017; Vierbuchen et al., 2017; Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This mechanistic description is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Mice lacking Arid1a in the colon develop adenocarcinomas.
source: For instance, mice lacking Arid1a, the DNA-binding SWI/SNF subunit, in the colon develop adenocarcinomas (Mathur et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Arid1a deletion can both impair and promote the initiation of liver tumorigenesis.
source: However, opposing and stage dependent roles have been described within the same tissue, as Arid1a deletion can both impair and promote the initiation of liver tumorigenesis (Fang et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2017) and accelerates progression and metastasis in established disease (Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Arid1a deletion accelerates progression and metastasis in established liver disease.
source: However, opposing and stage dependent roles have been described within the same tissue, as Arid1a deletion can both impair and promote the initiation of liver tumorigenesis (Fang et al., 2015; Sun et al., 2017) and accelerates progression and metastasis in established disease (Sun et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Smarca4 deletion accelerates tumor onset but slows progression in pancreatic tumorigenesis.
source: Another subunit, Smarca4, displays the opposite pattern in pancreatic tumorigenesis, where its deletion accelerates tumor onset but slows progression (Roy et al., 2015; von Figura et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: The role of various SWI/SNF complex components in tumor initiation and progression can be context dependent.
source: Thus, the role of various SWI/SNF complex components in tumor initiation and progression can be context dependent.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the examples of context-dependent effects cited in the preceding text.

claim: SWI/SNF complex dependent regulation of gene expression controls cell identity and differentiation in developmental as well as regenerative contexts.
source: Indeed, in drosophila and mammalian systems, SWI/SNF complex dependent regulation of gene expression controls cell identity and differentiation in developmental as well as regenerative contexts (Sun et al., 2016; Takada et al., 2016; Vieira et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Mutations in ARID1A or other SWI/SNF components occur in up to 25% of pancreatic cancer patients.
source: We set out to develop an in vivo model to address the role of the SWI/SNF component ARID1A in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), a setting in which mutations in ARID1A or other SWI/SNF components occur in up to 25% of cancer patients (Shain et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: PDAC is nearly invariably initiated by activating mutations in the KRAS oncogene.
source: PDAC is nearly invariably initiated by activating mutations in the KRAS oncogene (Bailey et al., 2016), while additional mutations in tumor suppressor genes are accumulated in the course of PDAC progression (Hezel et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Additional mutations in tumor suppressor genes are accumulated in the course of PDAC progression.
source: PDAC is nearly invariably initiated by activating mutations in the KRAS oncogene (Bailey et al., 2016), while additional mutations in tumor suppressor genes are accumulated in the course of PDAC progression (Hezel et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: PDAC can arise from mucinous precursor lesions, including pancreatic intra-epithelial neoplasia (PanIN), intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMN) and Mucinous Cystic Neoplasms (MCN).
source: PDAC can arise from mucinous precursor lesions, including the most common, pancreatic intra-epithelial neoplasia (PanIN), as well as intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMN) and Mucinous Cystic Neoplasms (MCN), with activating KRAS mutations frequently found in these early neoplastic stages (Hosoda et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Activating KRAS mutations are frequently found in early neoplastic stages of PDAC.
source: PDAC can arise from mucinous precursor lesions, including the most common, pancreatic intra-epithelial neoplasia (PanIN), as well as intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms (IPMN) and Mucinous Cystic Neoplasms (MCN), with activating KRAS mutations frequently found in these early neoplastic stages (Hosoda et al., 2017; Lee et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Tissue specific expression of mutant Kras in the developing and adult mouse pancreas recapitulates both the range of preneoplastic lesions and their progression to malignant PDAC.
source: Tissue specific expression of mutant Kras in the developing and adult mouse pancreas recapitulates both the range of preneoplastic lesions and their progression to malignant PDAC (Hingorani et al., 2005; Izeradjene et al., 2007; Sano et al., 2014; Siveke et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Lineage tracing studies indicate mutant Kras can drive PanIN development from acinar cells that undergo acinar to ductal metaplasia (ADM).
source: Lineage tracing studies indicate mutant Kras can drive PanIN development from acinar cells that undergo a process of persistent trans-differentiation termed acinar to ductal metaplasia (ADM) (Kopp et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In acinar to ductal metaplasia, acinar cells lose their pyramidal morphology, downregulate expression of digestive enzymes and TFs characteristic of acinar cells, and turn on an embryonic progenitor-like transcriptional program.
source: In this process, acinar cells lose their pyramidal morphology, downregulate expression of digestive enzymes and TFs characteristic of acinar cells, and turn on an embryonic progenitor-like transcriptional program that includes expression of ductal markers and development of glandular morphology (Storz, 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Deletion of key transcriptional regulators of acinar cell identity (Ptf1a, Nr5a2 and Pdx1), when combined with oncogenic Kras, accelerates ADM and PanIN development.
source: Deletion of key transcriptional regulators of acinar cell identity and regeneration such as Ptf1a, Nr5a2 and Pdx1, when combined with oncogenic Kras, accelerates ADM and PanIN development (Flandez et al., 2014b; Krah et al., 2015; Roy et al., 2016; Shi et al., 2009; von Figura et al., 2014b).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Maintenance of acinar cell identity and regenerative homeostasis provides an important barrier to tumorigenesis in PDAC.
source: Thus, maintenance of acinar cell identity and regenerative homeostasis provides an important barrier to tumorigenesis in PDAC.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the cited studies showing that loss of acinar identity accelerates tumorigenesis.

claim: A substantial portion of KC-RIK-shArid1a mice became moribund within two weeks of doxycycline administration.
source: Surprisingly, a substantial portion of shArid1a mice became moribund within two weeks of enrollment on dox chow, while shRen mice remained healthy (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is supported by survival data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Acute morbidity in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice was closely associated with high degree of chimerism (>95%).
source: Acute morbidity was closely associated with KC-RIK-shArid1a mice exhibiting a high degree of chimerism (>95%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), indicating that at some level normal unrecombined cells can compensate for the gross functional defects produced by Arid1a depletion in this context.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Normal unrecombined cells can compensate for the gross functional defects produced by Arid1a depletion.
source: Acute morbidity was closely associated with KC-RIK-shArid1a mice exhibiting a high degree of chimerism (>95%) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), indicating that at some level normal unrecombined cells can compensate for the gross functional defects produced by Arid1a depletion in this context.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that only high chimerism mice became moribund.

claim: Moribund KC-RIK-shArid1a mice exhibited marked steatorrhea.
source: Moribund mice exhibited marked steatorrhea (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating exocrine insufficiency as a possible cause of their failure to thrive.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Steatorrhea indicates exocrine insufficiency as a possible cause of failure to thrive in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice.
source: Moribund mice exhibited marked steatorrhea (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B), indicating exocrine insufficiency as a possible cause of their failure to thrive.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known relationship between steatorrhea and exocrine insufficiency.

claim: Arid1a knockdown induces dramatic remodeling of the exocrine pancreas with replacement by Alcian Blue, Sox9, and Cytokeratin 19 positive mucinous metaplastic lesions.
source: Consistent with decreased exocrine function, histological analyses revealed that Arid1a knockdown induces a dramatic remodeling of the exocrine pancreas compared to shRen mice. shArid1a exocrine parenchyma was predominantly replaced by Alcian Blue, Sox9, and Cytokeratin 19 positive mucinous metaplastic lesion (MMLs) (Figure 2B–D), characteristic of low-grade PanIN lesions (Figure 2C, Figure 2—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figures 2B-D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The increase in PanINs upon Arid1a knockdown was accompanied by a dramatic reduction in cells positive for the differentiated acinar cell marker Cpa1.
source: This increase in PanINs was accompanied by a dramatic reduction in cells positive for the differentiated acinar cell marker Cpa1 (Figure 2E,F), indicating a role for Arid1a in maintaining acinar cell identity in the setting of mutant Kras.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 2E and 2F.

claim: Arid1a plays a role in maintaining acinar cell identity in the setting of mutant Kras.
source: This increase in PanINs was accompanied by a dramatic reduction in cells positive for the differentiated acinar cell marker Cpa1 (Figure 2E,F), indicating a role for Arid1a in maintaining acinar cell identity in the setting of mutant Kras.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observed loss of acinar markers upon Arid1a suppression.

claim: Acinar cell depletion upon Arid1a knockdown was likely a consequence of accelerated acinar ductal reprogramming rather than acinar cell death.
source: Indeed, acinar cell depletion was likely a consequence of accelerated acinar ductal reprogramming rather than acinar cell death, since pancreata derived from shArid1a mice were not atrophied (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D), and showed similar levels of cleaved caspase three and Ki67 staining as controls (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing no atrophy and similar apoptosis/proliferation markers.

claim: Only 1 of 11 KC-RIK-shArid1a mice that survived past 1 year showed histological evidence of PDAC at time of sacrifice.
source: Of note, the Alcian blue-positive PanINs induced upon Arid1a silencing maintained low levels of Arid1a even after a year on dox chow (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A–C). Only 1 of 11 KC-RIK-shArid1a mice that survived past 1 year showed histological evidence of PDAC at time of sacrifice (Figure 2A), similar to historically reported rates of PDAC development in mice harboring Kras mutations in the absence of additional genetic events (Hingorani et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from long-term survival studies.

claim: The rate of PDAC development in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice is similar to historically reported rates in mice harboring Kras mutations alone.
source: Only 1 of 11 KC-RIK-shArid1a mice that survived past 1 year showed histological evidence of PDAC at time of sacrifice (Figure 2A), similar to historically reported rates of PDAC development in mice harboring Kras mutations in the absence of additional genetic events (Hingorani et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim compares the current data to published literature.

claim: While the ability of Arid1a to stabilize acinar cell identity may act as a barrier to pancreatic cancer initiation, other factors are likely necessary to promote the PanIN-to-PDAC transition.
source: Thus, while the ability of Arid1a to stabilize acinar cell identity may act as a barrier to pancreatic cancer initiation, other factors are likely necessary to promote the PanIN-to-PDAC transition.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that PanINs do not progress to PDAC at high rates.

claim: Acute loss of Arid1a in the setting of a pre-existing Kras mutation rapidly perturbs the identity and function of pancreatic acinar cells.
source: Collectively, our data suggest that acute loss of Arid1a in the setting of a pre-existing Kras mutation rapidly perturbs the identity and function of pancreatic acinar cells, enhancing their sensitivity to metaplastic and PanIN-inducing signals stemming from oncogenic Kras.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: C-RIK-shArid1a mice (without KrasG12D) did not become moribund following doxycycline administration.
source: To this end, we eliminated the LSL-KrasG12D allele from ES cell-derived KC-RIK-shArid1a and KC-RIK-shRen mice though one round of breeding. These C-RIK-shRNA mice were then placed on dox at five weeks of age, after the completion of pancreas development, as in the KC-RIK experiments. In contrast to settings involving oncogenic Kras, these mice did not become moribund following dox administration, and pancreata from both shArid1a and shRen mice appeared normal (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Pancreata from C-RIK-shArid1a mice (without KrasG12D) appeared normal despite Arid1a suppression.
source: In contrast to settings involving oncogenic Kras, these mice did not become moribund following dox administration, and pancreata from both shArid1a and shRen mice appeared normal (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: C-RIK-shArid1a mice retained expression of the acinar marker Cpa1 despite Arid1a knockdown.
source: Importantly, shArid1a mice harboring wild-type Kras retained expression of the acinar marker Cpa1 (Figure 3E,F), which was lost in the KrasG12D setting.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3E and 3F.

claim: No differences in markers of stressed acinar cells (Clusterin) or proliferation (Ki67) were noted in C-RIK-shArid1a mice compared to controls.
source: Similarly, no differences in markers of stressed acinar cells (Clusterin) or proliferation (Ki67) were noted (Figure 3E,G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 3E, 3G, and 3H.

claim: Arid1a is dispensable for maintenance of normal acinar cell identity.
source: Although subtle differences in cell morphology and the pattern of E-cadherin staining were noted in cells with reduced Arid1a levels, no pancreas degeneration or exocrine insufficiency was observed despite sustained Arid1a knockdown. Therefore, Arid1a is dispensable for maintenance of normal acinar cell identiy (Figure 3I, Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from long-term Arid1a suppression in the absence of Kras mutation.

claim: Arid1a suppression had no impact on caerulein-induced pancreatitis damage and regeneration program.
source: Arid1a suppression had no impact on this damage and regeneration program. At day two post-caerulein treatment, both C-RIK-shRen mice and C-RIK-shArid1a animals exhibited a similar increase in inflammation, ADM, and expression of acinar stress response genes (clusterin) and a concomitant decrease in expression of markers of acinar differentiation (Cpa1) (Figure 3J; and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C). Importantly, both inflammation and ADM were resolved to a similar degree by day nine in both genotypes (Figure 3—figure supplements 2A–C and 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from caerulein-induced pancreatitis experiments.

claim: Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity.
source: Thus, Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity. It is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation, but plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing Arid1a effects in different genetic contexts.

claim: Arid1a is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation.
source: Thus, Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity. It is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation, but plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
evidence: This claim is supported by the caerulein regeneration experiments.

claim: Arid1a plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
source: Thus, Arid1a function plays a genotype-specific role in dictating acinar cell identity. It is dispensable for restoring normal acinar differentiation following transient tissue damage and dedifferentiation, but plays an active role in preventing preneoplastic lineage specification driven by oncogenic Kras.
evidence: This claim is supported by the differential effects of Arid1a suppression in Kras mutant vs wild-type contexts.

claim: Previous work using traditional conditional mouse models showed that SWI/SNF subunits, when deleted concurrently with Kras activation, lead to decreased acinar sensitivity to Kras driven ADM and PanIN development.
source: Our results showing that Arid1a suppression accelerates Kras driven erosion of acinar identity are surprising in light of previous work using traditional conditional mouse models in which SWI/SNF subunits, when deleted concurrently with Kras activation, lead to decreased acinar sensitivity to Kras driven ADM and PanIN development (Kimura et al., 2018; von Figura et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the P5 cohort showed an accelerated reduction of acinar cells and increase in mucinous lesions resembling the adult phenotype.
source: KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the P5 cohort showed an accelerated reduction of eosinophilic acinar cells and a concomitant increase in mucinous lesions that were morphologically consistent with low grade-PanINs, resembling the adult phenotype (Figure 4C–E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the E7 cohort exhibited a striking retention of Cpa1+ acinar tissue.
source: In contrast, KC-RIK-shArid1a mice from the E7 cohort, while still displaying ADM/PanIN lesions, exhibited a striking retention of Cpa1+ acinar tissue (Figure 4C–E; Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), a feature that was not observed in either P5 or adult cohorts.
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4C-E and Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The retained acinar cells in the E7 cohort failed to upregulate the ductal markers CK19 and Sox9 in the presence of mutant Kras.
source: Moreover, despite efficient and comparable Arid1a knockdown in the different cohorts (Figure 4D, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B), the retained acinar cells observed in the E7 cohort failed to upregulate the ductal markers CK19 and Sox9 in the presence of mutant Kras (Figure 4G,H).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figures 4G and 4H.

claim: Arid1a suppression accelerates the transition from an acinar to a mucinous cell fate in the presence of a pre-existing oncogenic Kras mutation.
source: Thus, Arid1a suppression accelerates the transition from an acinar to a mucinous cell fate in the presence of a pre-existing oncogenic Kras mutation (adult and P5 cohorts) whereas, when occurring concomitant with KrasG12D activation, it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype (E7 cohort).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claim: When Arid1a suppression occurs concomitant with KrasG12D activation, it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype.
source: Thus, Arid1a suppression accelerates the transition from an acinar to a mucinous cell fate in the presence of a pre-existing oncogenic Kras mutation (adult and P5 cohorts) whereas, when occurring concomitant with KrasG12D activation, it paradoxically promotes retention of the acinar cell phenotype (E7 cohort).
evidence: This is a summary conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claim: Arid1a has a temporal, context-dependent role in regulating acinar identity in response to oncogenic Kras.
source: Taken together, these data reveal a temporal, context-dependent role for Arid1a in regulating acinar identity in response to oncogenic Kras.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claim: Arid1a restoration did not reverse the acinar reprogramming phenotype.
source: Remarkably, Arid1a restoration did not reverse the acinar reprogramming phenotype. As expected, pancreata from mice withdrawn from dox retained expression of the mKate2 lineage marker, but lost the shRNA-linked GFP fluorescence signal (Figure 5B). Staining of tissues from KC-RIK-shRen and -shArid1a animals for Arid1a showed partial restoration of Arid1a by 5 days after withdrawal and full restoration at 2 and 4 weeks (Figure 5C). Despite this, histological assessment of KC-RIK-shRen and -shArid1a mice after dox withdrawal showed retention of widespread mucinous lesions as in the on dox condition, without a reversal of the PanIN phenotype towards an acinar or even ADM cell fate (Figure 5D,E).
evidence: This claim is supported by data from doxycycline withdrawal experiments shown in Figures 5B-E.

claim: Arid1a loss enables a non-reversible reprogramming of cell fate that is dependent on cellular and genetic context.
source: Thus, Arid1a loss enables a non-reversible reprogramming of cell fate that is dependent on cellular and genetic context.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the irreversibility experiments.

claim: Principal component analysis of RNA-seq data indicated that the two shRNAs targeting Arid1a conferred a transcriptional profile distinct from that of the shRen animals.
source: Principal component analysis of RNA-seq data indicated that the two shRNAs targeting Arid1a conferred a transcriptional profile distinct from that of the shRen animals, confirming these shRNAs triggered minimal off-target effects (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The two Arid1a shRNAs triggered minimal off-target effects.
source: Principal component analysis of RNA-seq data indicated that the two shRNAs targeting Arid1a conferred a transcriptional profile distinct from that of the shRen animals, confirming these shRNAs triggered minimal off-target effects (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is inferred from the clustering of the two different Arid1a shRNAs together.

claim: Analysis of RNAseq data detected 711 downregulated and 505 upregulated genes upon Arid1a knockdown.
source: Further analysis of the RNAseq data using an FDR threshold of 0.05 detected 711 downregulated and 505 upregulated genes (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Notable changes upon Arid1a knockdown included a reduction in acinar-related digestive enzymes and an increase in cellular components needed for mucin production.
source: Among the notable changes were a reduction in acinar-related digestive enzymes and an increase in cellular components needed for the mucin production characteristic of PDAC precursor lesions.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data analysis.

claim: Gene set enrichment analysis revealed a general activation of a mucinous lesion transcriptional program after 5 days on dox.
source: Consistent with our histological findings, gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA) revealed a general activation of a mucinous lesion transcriptional program after 5 days on dox: genes that are decreased in PanIN organoids relative to normal organoids were also downregulated, while genes enriched in PanIN organoids were up in shArid1a pancreata as well (Figure 6D) (Boj et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6D.

claim: GSEA identified downregulation of genes associated with acinar function upon Arid1a knockdown.
source: In parallel with mucin upregulation characteristic of PanIN development in KC-RIK-shArid1a mice, GSEA identified downregulation of genes associated with acinar function, such as those encoding the digestive enzymes Cel, Klk1 and Amy1 (Hoang et al., 2016), which was confirmed by RT-PCR (Figure 6E).
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA and RT-PCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Significant downregulation of gene expression programs sustained by master acinar TFs (Nr5a2 and Ptf1a) was noted upon Arid1a knockdown.
source: Importantly, significant downregulation of gene expression programs sustained by master acinar TFs (Nr5a2 and Ptf1a) required to maintain acinar differentiation (Holmstrom et al., 2011; Jiang et al., 2016) (Figure 6D) were noted.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA data shown in Figure 6D.

claim: RNA-seq data did not show significant downregulation of the acinar TFs Nr5a2, Ptf1a or Mist1 themselves at the 5-day timepoint.
source: Interestingly, our RNA-seq data did not show significant downregulation of the acinar TFs Nr5a2, Ptf1a or Mist1 themselves at this timepoint (see Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The destabilization of acinar cell identity upon Arid1a suppression most likely results from impaired recruitment or function of acinar TFs at their appropriate targets.
source: Thus, the destablization of acinar cell identity that occurs upon Arid1a suppression in the setting of oncogenic Kras most likely results from impaired recruitment or function of these acinar TFs at their appropriate targets.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the observation that TF target genes are downregulated without changes in TF expression.

claim: Knockdown of Arid1a resulted in striking changes in chromatin accessibility, with shArid1a chromatin profiles clearly separated from shRen by PCA.
source: We found that knockdown of Arid1a resulted in striking changes in chromatin accessibility, with shArid1a chromatin profiles that clearly separated from shRen by PCA (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 7A and 7B.

claim: 50,000–60,000 dynamic peaks were observed upon Arid1a knockdown, virtually all of which were reduced in the shArid1a samples relative to the shRen controls.
source: 50,000–60,000 dynamic peaks were observed, virtually all of which were reduced in the shArid1a samples relative to the shRen controls (Figure 7B,C).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figures 7B and 7C.

claim: Arid1a-containing SWI/SNF complexes are required to maintain substantial regions of open chromatin in the pre-neoplastic pancreas.
source: This indicates that Arid1a-containing SWI/SNF complexes are required to maintain substantial regions of open chromatin in the pre-neoplastic pancreas.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the widespread loss of chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.

claim: The majority of dynamic sites upon Arid1a knockdown were located in intergenic regions or introns, while promoters displayed fewer dynamic peaks.
source: Interestingly, although the chromatin accessibility was highest around transcriptional start site (TSS) regions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A), the majority of dynamic sites were located in intergenic regions or introns, while promoters displayed fewer dynamic peaks (relative to the genome-wide distribution of total detectable peaks) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ATAC-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: The regions of reduced chromatin accessibility observed upon Arid1a knockdown likely include enhancers whose inactivation may be responsible for the altered transcriptional profiles.
source: In B cells, intergenic and intronic regions that are enriched for Brg1 binding and lost upon Brg1 ablation are associated with H3K4me1 bound enhancers essential for establishing B-cell fate (Bossen et al., 2015). Accordingly, we suspect that the regions of reduced chromatin accessibility observed upon Arid1a knockdown includes enhancers, whose inactivation may be ultimately responsible for the altered transcriptional profiles we observed.
evidence: This is an inference based on published literature about SWI/SNF function in other cell types.

claim: Binding motifs for several key acinar-specific TFs (Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Rbpj) were enriched in genomic regions losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.
source: In addition, and consistent with impact of Arid1a suppression on acinar cell fate, we identified enrichment of binding motifs for several key acinar-specific TFs (Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Rbpj) in the genomic regions losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: Binding motifs for Pdx1 were enriched in genomic regions losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.
source: These same sites also showed enrichment in binding motifs for Pdx1, a TF that constrains acinar identity during mutant Kras-driven PanIN development (Roy et al., 2016) (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is supported by motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: There was a significant enrichment of Nr5a2, Ptf1a, and Pdx1 binding sites at ATAC-seq peaks that lose accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown.
source: This analysis showed a significant enrichment of TF binding sites at ATAC-seq peaks that lose accessibility upon Arid1a knockdown compared with sites without loss of acessibility (Nr5a2 and Ptf1a: p<2.2e-16, Pdx1: p<0.0016; Fisher's exact test; see Figure 7E and a representative ATAC-Seq track for the acinar target Cela2a).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 target genes losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a suppression were significantly downregulated.
source: As shown in Figure 7F, Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 target genes losing chromatin accessibility upon Arid1a suppression were significantly downregulated in shArid1a vs. shRen mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 7F.

claim: Genes downregulated upon Arid1a suppression showed a significantly increased density of Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 binding sites losing chromatin accessibility compared to genes whose expression is upregulated or unchanged.
source: More globally, genes downregulated upon Arid1a suppression showed a significantly increased density of Nr5a2, Ptf1a and Pdx1 binding sites losing chromatin accessibility as compared to genes whose expression is upregulated or unchanged (Figure 7G; Mean peak density: downregulated genes 1.53, upregulated genes: 0.72, unchanged: 0.92; Welch's t test: p=2.55e-14 for down vs. upregulated genes, p=6.372e-11 for down vs. unchanged genes).
evidence: This claim is supported by statistical analysis shown in Figure 7G.

claim: Arid1a depletion results in loss of chromatin accessibility at acinar-specific enhancers, limiting the transcriptional output of acinar master TFs and the expression of transcriptional programs that direct acinar cell fate.
source: These data support a model whereby Arid1a depletion results in loss of chromatin accessibility at acinar-specific enhancers, limiting the transcriptional output of acinar master TFs and, consequently, the expression of transcriptional programs that direct acinar cell fate.
evidence: This is a mechanistic model inferred from the combined ATAC-seq and RNA-seq data.

claim: Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous, pancreatic cancer precursor lesions.
source: In this study, we used a rapid and robust mouse-modeling platform to study the consequences of inducible and reversible suppression of the Arid1a SWI/SNF subunit in a mouse model of pancreatic cancer. Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous, pancreatic cancer precursor lesions that cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression.
evidence: This is a summary of the main findings of the study.

claim: Mucinous pancreatic cancer precursor lesions induced by Arid1a suppression cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression.
source: Suppression of Arid1a in adult acinar cells harboring oncogenic Kras mutations accelerates acinar to ductal reprogramming and specification of mucinous, pancreatic cancer precursor lesions that cannot be reversed by restoring endogenous Arid1a expression.
evidence: This is a summary of the irreversibility findings.

claim: Arid1a can provide a potent barrier to Kras driven acinar to ductal metaplasia and early stage pancreatic neoplasia.
source: Thus, our data suggest that Arid1a can provide a potent barrier to Kras driven acinar to ductal metaplasia and, consequently, early stage pancreatic neoplasia.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data.

claim: Once disrupted by Arid1a mutation, altered cells are reprogrammed in such a manner that Arid1a is no longer needed to sustain the aberrant cell fate.
source: Once disrupted by Arid1a mutation, these altered cells are reprogrammed in such a manner that Arid1a is no longer needed to sustain the aberrant cell fate.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the irreversibility experiments.

claim: The phenotype produced by Arid1a depletion in the presence of oncogenic Kras is characterized by reduced chromatin accessibility accompanied by loss of acinar morphology, reduced expression of acinar genes, and upregulation of a signature characteristic of mucinous lesions.
source: The phenotype produced by Arid1a depletion in the presence of an oncogenic Kras mutation is characterized by reduced chromatin accessibility accompanied by loss of acinar morphology, reduced expression of acinar genes, and upregulation of a signature characteristic of mucinous lesions.
evidence: This is a summary of the molecular and cellular phenotypes observed.

claim: Genomic areas rendered accessible by Arid1a harbor elements involved in preventing acinar to duct like trans-differentiation in the context of mutant Kras.
source: These features imply that genomic areas rendered accessible by Arid1a harbor elements involved in preventing acinar to duct like trans-differentiation in the context of mutant Kras, a critical rate-limiting step in Kras driven pancreatic neoplasia.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the chromatin accessibility and gene expression data.

claim: Arid1a disruption, in the presence of oncogenic Kras, reduces the chromatin accessibility of key TFs to the enhancers of genes needed to sustain acinar cell fate.
source: Indeed, our transcriptional and chromatin profiling data imply that Arid1a disruption, in the presence of oncogenic Kras, reduces the chromatin accessibility of key TFs to the enhancers of genes needed to sustain acinar cell fate.
evidence: This is a mechanistic conclusion drawn from the combined transcriptional and chromatin profiling data.

claim: Nr5a2 can physically interact with the SWI/SNF complex via the Baf60 subunit.
source: At least one such factor, Nr5a2, can physically interact with the SWI/SNF complex via the Baf60 subunit (Debril et al., 2004), suggesting a possible mechanism for aberrant Nr5a2 target deregulation upon Arid1a loss.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The accelerated PanIN formation produced by Arid1a suppression required the presence of a Kras mutation.
source: The accelerated PanIN formation produced by Arid1a suppression required the presence of a Kras mutation, the initiating event in pancreatic carcinogenesis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing Arid1a effects in Kras mutant vs wild-type contexts.

claim: Arid1a suppression in the normal pancreas did not appreciably perturb acinar differentiation, even during wound healing responses.
source: Thus, Arid1a suppression in the normal pancreas did not appreciably perturb acinar differentiation, even during wound healing responses that force a reversible acinar to ductal metaplasia.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings from experiments in the absence of Kras mutation.

claim: Arid1a suppression sensitizes pancreatic epithelial cells to mucinous reprogramming by oncogenic Kras or increases the efficiency of Kras-induced acinar-to-ADM-to-PanIN transitions.
source: Apparently, Arid1a suppression sensitizes pancreatic epithelial cells to mucinous reprogramming by oncogenic Kras or, alternatively, increases the efficiency of Kras-induced acinar-to-ADM-to-PanIN transitions.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the mechanism by which Arid1a loss cooperates with Kras.

claim: The Kras-dependence of Arid1a suppression effects differs from the phenotype produced by deletion of acinar TFs such as Ptf1a or Nr5a2.
source: Regardless, this Kras-dependence differs from the phenotype produced by deletion of acinar TFs such as Ptf1a or Nr5a2, whose loss generally perturbs acinar maintenance and/or regeneration (Cobo et al., 2018; Flandez et al., 2014a; Krah et al., 2015; von Figura et al., 2014b).
evidence: This comparison is based on published literature about acinar TF deletions.

claim: The potent and cooperative effects between oncogenic signaling and chromatin remodeling at eroding barriers to cellular plasticity contributes to the high frequency of SWI/SNF component inactivation in many cancer types.
source: We hypothesize that the potent and cooperative effects between oncogenic signaling and chromatin remodeling at eroding barriers to cellular plasticity contributes to the high frequency of SWI/SNF component inactivation in many cancer types.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed based on the findings of the study.

claim: Deletion of Brg1 during pancreatic development in conjunction with oncogenic Kras results in the formation of IPMN-like lesions.
source: Deletion of Brg1 during pancreatic development in conjunction with oncogenic Kras results in the formation of IPMN-like lesions contiguous with the native duct system that may derive from the ductal compartment rather than through ADM.
evidence: This claim is based on published literature about Brg1 deletion.

claim: Elimination of Brg1 in adult acinar cells prevents the development of Kras driven acinar to duct-like transdifferentiation and PanIN development.
source: Furthermore elimination of Brg1 in adult acinar cells prevents the development of Kras driven acinar to duct-like transdifferentiation and PanIN development (von Figura et al., 2014a).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: A recent study employing conditional deletion of Arid1a in the pancreas observed IPMN formation but PanIN formation was not suppressed.
source: While a recent study employing conditional deletion of Arid1a in the pancreas also observed IPMN formation, PanIN formation was not suppressed, pointing towards distinct molecular consequences of targeting different SWI/SNF components (Kimura et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: The striking predominance of PanINs over IPMNs in the KC-RIK-shArid1a model may be due to a dosage effect.
source: The striking predominance of PanINs over IPMNs in our model may be due to a dosage effect, where IPMN formation requires complete loss of Arid1a in ductal progenitors or ductal cells, while acinar cells expressing mutant Kras are more highly dependent on Arid1a to maintain their identity, and thus are rapidly reprogrammed to mucinous PanINs upon partial Arid1a suppression.
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for the observed phenotype.

claim: The timing of SWI/SNF perturbation can have a dramatic effect on tumorigenesis phenotypes.
source: While the distinct molecular consequences of different SWI/SNF component mutations may contribute to phenotypic variability in other aspects of PDAC progression, these observations indicate that the timing of SWI/SNF perturbation can have a dramatic effect on tumorigenesis phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal cohort experiments.

claim: The fact that Arid1a suppression can produce distinct phenotypes depending on the timing of gene suppression has ramifications for studying the SWI/SNF complex in other cancer types and for cancer modeling in the mouse.
source: Regardless of the precise mechanism, the fact that Arid1a suppression can produce distinct phenotypes depending on the timing of gene suppression has ramifications for studying the SWI/SNF complex in other cancer types and, more generally, for cancer modeling in the mouse.
evidence: This is a broader implication drawn from the findings.

claim: Human cancers evolve as a consequence of a stepwise accumulation of mutations rather than the acquisition of multiple mutations simultaneously.
source: Indeed, human cancers evolve as a consequence of a stepwise accumulation of mutations rather than the acquisition of multiple mutations simultaneously.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cancer evolution.

claim: Some phenotypes attributed to particular gene mutation in mice may not always extrapolate to the human system because of the differential consequences of the timing of genetic events.
source: Consequently, some phenotypes attributed to particular gene mutation in mice may not always extrapolate to the human system – not because of species differences, but because of the differential consequences of the timing of genetic events.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the limitations of traditional mouse models.

claim: The inducible shRNA technology used in this study has been optimized to produce gene suppression that approaches that produced by gene deletion.
source: Indeed, the inducible shRNA technology used herein has been optimized to produce gene suppression that approaches that produced by gene deletion (Bolden et al., 2014; Dow et al., 2015; Ebbesen et al., 2016; Hemann et al., 2003; Premsrirut et al., 2011) yet, by leaving the target locus intact, enables the endogenous protein to be re-expressed upon shRNA silencing.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: shRNA mediated knockdown of Arid1a produced a shift in acinar to mucinous cell fate and a PanIN histopathology that was not reversed by subsequent Arid1a re-expression.
source: Here, shRNA mediated knockdown of Arid1a produced a shift in acinar to mucinous cell fate and a PanIN histopathology that was not reversed by subsequent Arid1a re-expression.
evidence: This is a summary of the irreversibility findings.

claim: The irreversibility of Arid1a-induced phenotypes stands in contrast to what has been noted for other tumor suppressor genes like APC in colon cancer models.
source: Such results suggest that ectopic overexpression studies in cell lines with mutations in SWI/SNF components may not reflect the biological activity of that component during tumor evolution. Furthermore, they stand in contrast to what has been noted for other tumor suppressor genes, for example, in colon cancer models where reversible APC suppression promoted the expansion of undifferentiated cells that readily underwent differentiation upon APC restoration (Dow et al., 2015).
evidence: This comparison is based on published literature about APC.

claim: ARID1A controls the expression of thousands of gene targets via interaction with available TFs.
source: Since ARID1A controls the expression of thousands of gene targets via interaction with available TFs (Kadoch and Crabtree, 2015; Kelso et al., 2017; Mathur et al., 2017; Sun et al., 2016), it is possible that factors absent from mucinous lesions might be needed to reestablish an acinar transcriptional program when Arid1a is restored.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Expression of the bHLH protein E47 in PDAC cells induces expression of digestive enzymes and activates a Mist1-based transcriptional network.
source: Although KrasG12D itself prevents acinar regeneration after pancreatitis-induced ADM, expression of the bHLH protein E47 in PDAC cells induces expression of digestive enzymes and activates a Mist1-based transcriptional network, indicating that such a reversion is possible (Kim et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Arid1a plays a role in the early stages of PDAC.
source: Taken together, our data identify a role for Arid1a in the early stages of PDAC.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion of the study.

claim: Initiating oncogenic KRAS mutations trigger ADM and PanIN conversion at low efficiency; mutation of ARID1A may boost the frequency of this process by increasing cellular plasticity.
source: This supports a model where initiating oncogenic KRAS mutations trigger ADM and PanIN conversion at low efficiency; mutation of ARID1A may boost the frequency of this process by increasing cellular plasticity.
evidence: This is a model proposed based on the findings of the study.

claim: The irreversibility of the Kras-induced PanIN phenotype indicates that impaired SWI/SNF function may not be required for tumor maintenance.
source: While studies to explore the role of ARID1A in later stage PDAC progression are in progress, the irreversibility of the Kras-induced PanIN phenotype indicates that impaired SWI/SNF function may not be required for tumor maintenance.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the irreversibility experiments.

claim: The identification of genotype-specific dependencies produced by SWI/SNF dysfunction rather than restoration of its normal activity may be a more effective way to exploit SWI/SNF mutations for new therapeutic approaches.
source: If confirmed, the identification of genotype-specific dependencies produced by SWI/SNF dysfunction rather than restoration of its normal activity may be a more effective way to exploit SWI/SNF mutations for new therapeutic approaches.
evidence: This is a therapeutic implication drawn from the findings.

claim: Some proposed vulnerabilities of SWI/SNF mutant cancers, such as ARID1B, extend across multiple tissues and mutational landscapes.
source: While some proposed vulnerabilities, such as ARID1B, extend across multiple tissues and mutational landscapes (Helming et al., 2014), our data imply that many such dependencies are likely to be limited to a particular cell type or co-mutation context, due to the high degree of context specificity of Arid1a function in regulating cell identity and plasticity.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: Many dependencies produced by SWI/SNF dysfunction are likely to be limited to a particular cell type or co-mutation context.
source: While some proposed vulnerabilities, such as ARID1B, extend across multiple tissues and mutational landscapes (Helming et al., 2014), our data imply that many such dependencies are likely to be limited to a particular cell type or co-mutation context, due to the high degree of context specificity of Arid1a function in regulating cell identity and plasticity.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the context-dependent effects of Arid1a observed in the study.

claim: The Ptf1a-Cre allele used in this study becomes activated in multi-potent pancreas progenitors at embryonic day 9.5 and remains active in acinar but not islet and ductal cells of the pancreas.
source: The Ptf1a-Cre allele used in this study becomes activated in multi-potent pancreas progenitors at embryonic day 9.5 and remains active in acinar but not islet and ductal cells of the pancreas (Kawaguchi et al., 2002).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published literature.

claim: In the KC-RIK model, Cre recombination occurs most commonly in acinar cells, but leaves some ducts and endocrine cells un-recombined.
source: Thus in our model, Cre recombination occurs most commonly in acinar cells, but leaves some ducts and endocrine cells un-recombined, as indicated by their lack of mKate2 staining.
evidence: This is an observation about the specificity of the Cre system used.

claim: The ES cell system used enables the direct production of experimental cohorts of chimeric mice harboring multiple alleles, dramatically accelerating the rate of experimentation while reducing animal waste.
source: This ES cell system enables the direct production of experimental cohorts of chimeric mice harboring multiple alleles, thereby dramatically accelerating the rate of experimentation while simultaneously reducing animal waste as byproducts of strain intercrossing (Dow et al., 2012; Premsrirut et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature describing the ES cell system.
